claims.text: The proposed intervention is LPBF of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi using a build-platform temperature of approximately 600 °C.
LPBF ordinarily involves high temperature gradients and rapid quenching around the melt pool.
Preheating the substrate to approximately 600 °C will reduce the temperature differential and thermal gradients during layer solidification relative to a room-temperature substrate.
Substrate preheating will moderate the cooling rate and reduce thermal shock.
Reduced thermal gradients will reduce residual stress in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Slower cooling and reduced thermal gradients will suppress solute segregation in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Lower temperature gradients can contribute to fewer LPBF defects.
Preheating will produce a more uniform AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Samples built on a preheated substrate will have a statistically significant reduction in residual stress relative to room-temperature LPBF samples.
Samples built on a preheated substrate will have a statistically significant reduction in compositional segregation relative to room-temperature LPBF samples.
Samples built on a preheated substrate will have lower defect density than room-temperature LPBF samples.
Substrate preheating will improve the yield strength of LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate preheating will improve the ductility of LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed effect is expected to hold over a build-platform temperature range of 500–650 °C.
Excessive substrate preheating may cause grain coarsening or unwanted phase transformations.
